proposal: The Mandate recommends that CMS launch a Medicaid personal option so families can use Medicaid dollars for coverage outside Medicaid; that Congress let states fund a private insurance benefit through a flexible account with catastrophic coverage; that CMS allow benefit redesign without waivers (dropping obsolete mandates, private-market-level benefits for able-bodied adults, long-term care redesign); and that payment reforms proceed without waivers or state plan amendments, with Section 1115 requirements added for work requirements and rescinded for non-health benefits such as climate-related services (pp. 468 to 469).

SMD #26-003 implements section 71118 (new Social Security Act section 1115(g)): Chief Actuary certification of budget neutrality before approval of new applications, amendments or renewals from 2027-01-01, and creates no personal option, account or waiver-free process. The 2026-07-07 bulletin rescinds the 2015 fast-track extension process, citing time needed for the certification.

status_summary: CMS rescinded its guidance on Medicaid coverage of health-related social needs on 2025-03-04, a step in the direction of the text's call to rescind Section 1115 requirements for non-health benefits. Public Law 119-21 (2025-07-04) set statutory community engagement requirements and a Section 1115 budget neutrality certification from 2027-01-01; CMS issued State Medicaid Director Letter #26-003 on 2026-06-11 on the certification, and on 2026-07-07 CMS ended fast-track review of Section 1115 extensions in light of it, which adds to rather than removes waiver process. No personal option, private insurance account option, waiver-free benefit redesign or waiver-free payment reform was found.

timeline.event: CMS issued an informational bulletin rescinding its November 2023 and December 2024 bulletins on Medicaid and CHIP coverage of health-related social needs and stopped relying on the related framework; future state requests are to be reviewed case by case.

Public Law 119-21 was approved, including community engagement requirements for expansion adults (section 71119) and a budget neutrality certification for Section 1115 demonstrations (section 71118), both effective 2027-01-01.
CMS issues State Medicaid Director Letter #26-003 on budget neutrality and Chief Actuary certification for Section 1115 demonstrations under section 71118, applying from 2027-01-01.
CMS rescinded its 2015 fast-track review process for Section 1115 demonstration extensions, citing the new budget neutrality certification requirement.

title: Medicaid personal option, private insurance accounts, flexible benefits and fewer waivers

The 2025-03-04 and 2026-07-07 bulletins and State Medicaid Director Letter #26-003 were read in full on the medicaid.gov host; the 2025 bulletin does not say how existing state approvals are affected. Section 71118 is confirmed by name in those CMS documents and section numbers against the GovInfo table of contents; the statute body is unreadable on GovInfo. Work requirements are tracked in c14-05 and financing in c14-06; this record counts only the personal option, account, benefit flexibility and waiver-process elements.
